cover.headline: A steady acute franchise whose EPS resets on tax in FY27; on the street's P/E method, with the pharma re-rating applied, we see {{dcf.upside|chg}}, but the market has not yet granted Alkem that premium
cover.lead: Alkem is India's #6 drug maker and #1 in antibiotics (67% of revenue from India), with a US generics arm (20%) and three young bets: Enzene biosimilars and contract manufacturing, MedTech (55% of Occlutech from Jul-2026) and generic semaglutide. Q1FY27 revenue rose 11% to ₹3,740 cr and EBITDA 4%, but profit fell 22% as the tax rate jumped to 32% when the Sikkim tax holiday ended; on the same day the USFDA's OAI on the Daman plant (45% of US sales) was disclosed. We forecast EPS to shareholders of ₹183.5 / 211.2 / 244.4 for FY27-29E, below FY26's ₹204.1 in FY27 and below consensus. Every broker note since Q1FY27 that discloses a method uses **P/E** (Nuvama's last public note, Nov-2025, used a sum of the parts), and so do we: **29.5x Sep-28E EPS (₹227.8)**, i.e. Alkem's 26.6x median forward P/E since Apr-2021 (EPS before exceptional items) lifted 10.25% for the pharma sector's re-rating, gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹7,215; DCF ₹4,649. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: #1 in anti-infectives for 15+ years, #3 by prescriptions, 17 brands above ₹100 cr (52% of domestic sales), 14,500+ reps and #1-2 in trade generics. Branded India grew ~12% in Q1FY27, 100bp ahead of the market on IQVIA. Net cash ₹5,764 cr; dividends ~25-30% of profit.

arguments.h: But growth is market-plus, not more, and FY27 EPS falls
arguments.p: Alkem's lead therapies (antibiotics, gastro, pain, vitamins) grew 4-9% market-wide in FY26; chronic is only ~22-23% of branded sales. The tax rate goes from 18% to ~31% (Sikkim holiday over), so FY27E EPS (₹183.5) is −10% on FY26 even with EBITDA +10%.

arguments.h: The new bets and the US cost more than they earn today
arguments.p: Enzene's New Jersey CDMO spends ~₹60 cr a quarter and breaks even only at $25-30mn of sales (FY28); Occlutech runs at breakeven; US sales are flat in dollars and Daman, which makes 45% of them, is under an OAI. Governance is AMBER: founder in his mid-80s, CEO seat empty, high promoter pay, steady promoter selling.

arguments.h: Valuation: the house method says cheap; the market disagrees
arguments.p: At ₹5,164 Alkem trades at 24.5x our FY28E EPS against a 26.6x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021, and its trailing P/E is −7% vs its five-year median while pharma peers are +10.25%. Our 29.5x applies the sector's move (house rule, no blend with Alkem's own); on Alkem's own move the value would be ~₹5,700 (HOLD). The DCF (₹4,649) is the warning.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): tax rate vs the 30-32% guidance, gross margin as costlier API flows through, trade-generics recovery, the first Occlutech quarter.
USFDA: progress on the Daman (Amaliya) OAI; any re-inspection, or escalation to a warning letter; the delayed US denosumab biosimilar approval.
US launches: generic tolvaptan (Q2FY27, limited competition); Enzene US CDMO contract wins towards the $25-30mn breakeven run-rate.
People: appointment of a new CEO; further promoter-group sales after the Jun-2026 block (90-day lock-up).
Monthly IQVIA data: whether branded growth stays ~1pp above the market; semaglutide share as prices fall.

sections.title: India's #6 drug maker: an acute-medicine franchise (antibiotics, antacids, pain, vitamins) with a US generics arm and three new bets

blocks.p: Alkem sells medicines. Two-thirds of revenue (₹9,851 cr of ₹14,712 cr in FY26) comes from India, where it is the 6th-largest company by value (~4.1% market share), 3rd by number of prescriptions and #1 in anti-infectives (antibiotics) for more than 15 years. Its biggest brands treat short, common illnesses: Pan (pantoprazole for acidity; the IPM's #2 brand family), Clavam and Taxim (antibiotics), A to Z (vitamins), Pan-D. These are "acute" therapies: patients take them for days, not years. About 22-23% of branded sales are "chronic" (diabetes, nerves, skin, breathing), where Alkem is a mid-ranked player. It also sells unbranded "trade generics" through distributors to chemists at low prices (it is #1 or #2 in that channel; moved into a subsidiary, Alkem Wellness, in FY26). Outside India, the US is 20% of revenue (192 generic applications filed, two plants in India and one API plant in California serve it), and other international markets (Australia, Chile, Germany, the UK, the Philippines and others) are 12%. On top sit three new bets, all loss-making or small today: Enzene (biosimilars and contract manufacturing of antibodies), Alkem MedTech (orthopaedic implants; 55% of Occlutech, a German heart-device maker, from Jul-2026) and generic semaglutide.

blocks.callout: **So what:** Alkem is a distribution and brand company built on acute medicines, sold by 14,500+ representatives and a large trade-generics network. That is a solid, cash-generative core, but acute is the slow half of the Indian market. The strategic question for the next five years is whether the chronic push and the new bets (biosimilars, CDMO, MedTech) can add growth faster than they absorb capital and management attention.

sections.title: From a 1973 Mumbai start-up to ₹14,700 cr of revenue: a family company that diversified late

blocks.p: Brothers Samprada Singh and Basudeo Narain (B.N.) Singh, from Bihar, founded Alkem in Mumbai in 1973 as a distributor-turned-manufacturer. It built its name on antibiotics (Taxim was the first Indian anti-infective brand to cross ₹100 cr, in 2006) and on a wide rural and semi-urban reach. It went abroad in 2007-12 (first US filing 2007; Ascend Laboratories in the US and Pharmacor in Australia, 2010; a US API plant, 2012) and bought Enzene Biosciences (2011) as a biosimilars start-up. The Dec-2015 IPO at ₹1,050 was an offer for sale: the company raised nothing. Samprada Singh died in 2019; B.N. Singh, now in his mid-80s, is still Executive Chairman, and the next generations of both branches sit on the Board. The last three years brought the biggest strategic shift since the 2010s: a US biologics plant, a MedTech arm, the trade-generics carve-out and the Occlutech purchase.

blocks.callout: **Our read:** for 45 years Alkem was a focused, conservative, family-run acute franchise. Since FY24 it has diversified into three capital-hungry adjacencies at once (US CDMO, MedTech, Occlutech) while the founder generation hands over and the first professional CEO has left. None of the new pieces is big enough yet to change the numbers, but together they explain why EBITDA margins did not expand in Q1FY27 despite a record gross margin.

sections.title: The Indian drug market: ~₹2.15 lakh crore, growing 9-12%, but Alkem's four big therapies grew only 4-9% in FY26

blocks.p: The Indian pharmaceutical market (IPM) was ~₹2.15 lakh crore at chemist level in FY26 (IQVIA SSA MAT Mar-26; cardiac ₹30,287 cr = 14.1%) and grew 9.0%; growth rose to 12.2% in the Jun-2026 quarter (acute 10.1%, chronic 15.4%), helped by generic semaglutide after its Mar-2026 patent expiry. Alkem's four biggest therapies are acute and grew slowly market-wide in FY26: anti-infectives +4.0%, gastro +5.7%, pain +7.2%, VMN +9.2%; the fast lanes were cardiac +13.8%, anti-diabetic +11.5% and respiratory +11.3%. Growth comes from three parts that move differently: price (Alkem: ~6% in Q1FY27; scheduled drugs under the Drug Price Control Order can rise only with wholesale inflation), new products (~3%) and volume (~2%). The mix is shifting to chronic therapies (cardiac, diabetes, respiratory, nerves) as lifestyle diseases rise and diagnosis improves. Policy pushes the other way on old acute molecules: price caps, the 2024 Uniform Code for Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices (UCPMP: no gifts, travel or cash to doctors), and government generic stores (Jan Aushadhi) and trade generics that undercut branded prices.

sections.title: Does the market's growth reach Alkem? In branded India, yes (slightly ahead of the market); in trade generics and the US, no

blocks.p: In FY26 Alkem grew 9.2% in India on IQVIA data against a market growing 9.0%: acute 8.5% (market 6.8%), chronic 12.6% (12.5%). In Q1FY27 it grew 13.2% vs 12.2% (acute 12.3% vs 10.1%; chronic 17.9% vs 15.4%) and beat the market in seven focus therapies (pain 1.8x, respiratory and derma 1.6x, VMN and anti-diabetic 1.4x, gastro 1.2x, anti-infectives 1.1x). Reported India sales grew only 10.3% because trade generics, which IQVIA does not track, were flat (Alkem cut credit days and raised prices after API inflation). Branded generics grew ~12%. The field force grew by ~1,450 people in FY26 (AR), mostly in chronic divisions, with attrition at 18-19%.

sections.title: India: #1 in antibiotics for 15 years, #6 overall; growth is market-plus in branded and flat in trade generics

blocks.p: India brought in ₹9,851 cr in FY26 (+9.7%) and ₹2,498 cr in Q1FY27 (+10.3%). It has three parts. (1) **Branded acute medicines** (~77% of branded sales): anti-infectives, gastro, pain and vitamins, where Alkem ranks #1, #4, #3 and #2. Its 17 brands above ₹100 cr make up 52% of domestic sales; Pan is the IPM's #2 brand family and Clavam rose to #9 in FY26. Leadership is real but the lanes are slow: the anti-infectives market grew 4% in FY26. (2) **Branded chronic** (~22-23%, rising ~1pp a year): anti-diabetic (empagliflozin combinations after their FY25 patent expiry, where Alkem is top-four; semaglutide since Mar-2026), CNS, derma, urology and inhaled respiratory. Alkem grows 1.4-1.6x the market here but ranks only #8-#19. (3) **Trade generics**: unbranded medicines sold to distributors at low prices. Alkem is #1 or #2, but "a lot of big guys have entered" (MD); growth was ~4% in FY26 after the carve-out into Alkem Wellness and flat in Q1FY27, when Alkem cut credit days and raised prices for API inflation. The MD would be "happy with late single digits" there.

sections.title: US generics: growth from the rupee and one launch a year; the Daman OAI puts 45% of US sales under a cloud

blocks.p: The US brought in ₹2,985 cr in FY26 (+20.3%, lifted by the limited-competition launch of generic sacubitril-valsartan in Q2FY26) and ₹744 cr in Q1FY27 (+6.5%). Underneath, the business is ex-growth: Alkem has filed 192 ANDAs and won 170 approvals (18 tentative), launched 11 products in Q1FY27, but "we really don't have volume growth" in recent launches (MD); price erosion has "bottomed out" at close to flat. FY27 guidance is "high single digit to mid", helped by the weaker rupee, with generic tolvaptan (a four-player market) launching in Q2. The bigger issue is quality: the USFDA inspected the Amaliya, Daman formulations plant from 20-Apr to 1-May-2026, issued a Form 483 with seven observations and classified the site **Official Action Indicated (OAI)** in Aug-2026. About 45% of US sales come from Daman. Supplies continue and management hopes to clear it in 6-12 months, but an OAI usually means no new approvals from the site until it is resolved, and it can escalate to a warning letter.

sections.title: Other markets grow 25-35%; Enzene and MedTech are options that lose money today

blocks.p: **Other international** (₹1,696 cr in FY26, +26.7%; ₹479 cr in Q1FY27, +34.5%): branded and generic sales in Australia (Pharmacor), Chile, Germany (+35-40%), the UK, France, Mexico, South Africa and Asia through Ascend and Pharmacor subsidiaries, plus biosimilar partner supplies. Management guides higher-teens growth; the base is small and the rupee helps. **Enzene Biosciences** (Alkem 88.99% fully diluted) has two arms: biosimilars (eight products in India, ~₹150 cr a year, profitable; denosumab approved in Europe through partner Theramex; the US denosumab approval missed its goal date after a 6-observation pre-approval inspection at Chakan in Feb-2026) and a monoclonal-antibody CDMO in Pune and Hopewell, New Jersey. Revenue ₹492.3 cr, loss ₹150.5 cr (AR FY26 note 3.37); US CDMO revenue under ₹100 cr in FY26. The US plant costs ~₹60 cr a quarter and needs $25-30mn of annual sales to break even, which the MD now expects in FY28, not within 12 months. In Feb-2026 outside investors (F-Prime, ERVI) put ₹26 cr into Enzene at ₹468.60 a share, which values 100% of it at ~₹2,817 cr (GAM calculation). No IPO or listing plan for Enzene was announced by 30-Sep-2026 (none found in filings or calls). **Alkem MedTech**: orthopaedic implants (Bombay Ortho, Adroit; ~₹50 cr of sales, small losses) and, from mid-Jul-2026, 55% of **Occlutech**. CY24 revenue €43mn; CY25E revenue ~€49mn, EBITDA ~€2mn, net loss ~€6.8mn (MOSL company update, 18-Feb-2026). Management targets ~₹400 cr of sales in FY27 at breakeven EBITDA, then +7-8pp of margin a year.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** Alkem has a narrow moat: prescriber habits for its big acute brands and a distribution reach that few can match make its India franchise durable and cash-generative. But the moat protects slow-growing categories, it is not deep in chronic, and the US business is a price-taker with a live regulatory problem. The tax advantage that flattered returns for a decade is gone. This is a good business priced as a growth business only if the sector premium applies to it.

sections.title: Revenue up 1.8x since FY20 and profit 2x; margins swung from 14% to 22% and back to ~20%; FY27 EPS falls on tax

blocks.p: Alkem's revenue grew from ₹8,344 cr in FY20 to ₹14,712 cr in FY26 (9.9% a year): India from ~₹5,450 cr to ₹9,851 cr (~10% a year), the US from ~₹2,200 cr to ₹2,985 cr (5% a year, with a dip in FY25) and other international markets from ~₹700 cr to ₹1,696 cr. Profit to shareholders doubled, from ₹1,127 cr to ₹2,302 cr, but not in a straight line. FY23 was a bad year: US price erosion, raw-material inflation and ₹173 cr of exceptional charges cut the EBITDA margin to 14.0% and EPS to ₹82 (₹138 in FY22). Since then the margin has rebuilt to 20.4% and EPS to ₹192.5 reported, ₹204.1 before exceptional items. Two things kept profit growth above revenue growth for a decade: Sikkim tax holidays (tax rate 9-18%) and rising treasury income. The first ends in FY27.

What changes in FY27 is tax: the rate jumps from 18% to 30-32%, so EPS to shareholders falls to ₹183.5 on our numbers even though EBITDA grows ~10%. From that lower base we model EPS of ₹211.2 / ₹244.4 for FY28-29E (6% a year from FY26's ₹204.1 before exceptional items).

sections.title: Gross margin at a ten-year high, EBITDA margin flat: new businesses eat the gain; the tax holiday is over

blocks.p: Alkem's gross margin (revenue less materials) rose from 59-64% in FY25 to 67.9% in Q1FY27, the best in ten years (MOSL), helped by fewer low-margin trade-generic sales, a weak rupee on export prices and old, cheaper API inventory. Little of it reached EBITDA: the Q1FY27 EBITDA margin was 20.5% against 21.9% a year earlier, because employee costs rose 16.7% (about 1,200 more medical representatives, increments and the new US plant) and other expenses 25.3% (the Enzene US plant's ~₹60 cr a quarter of running costs, Occlutech due diligence, overseas costs at a weaker rupee). Management guides a 66.5-67% gross margin for the rest of FY27 as costlier API flows through, and 20-21% EBITDA before Occlutech. Q4 is always weak (14.4% in Q4FY26, 12.4% in Q4FY25) because R&D filings bunch there and Indian sales are seasonally low.

blocks.p: Alkem reported Q1FY27 on 14-Aug-2026. Revenue rose 10.9% to ₹3,740 cr: India +10.3% (branded ~12%, trade generics flat), US +6.5%, other international +34.5%. Gross margin hit 67.9% (+260bp), but EBITDA rose only 3.7% to ₹766 cr (margin 20.5%, −145bp) as staff costs rose 16.7% and other expenses 25.3%. sections.title: Capital allocation: steady dividends, rising cash, and a turn towards riskier bets (US CDMO, MedTech)

blocks.p: Alkem turns most of its profit into cash: cash from operations was ₹5,824 cr over FY24-26, against ₹1,552 cr of capex and ₹1,659 cr of dividends. The dividend is ~25-30% of profit (FY26: ₹53 a share, ₹634 cr). The rest piled up as deposits and bonds (gross treasury ₹7,160 cr at Mar-26). What has changed is where the spare money goes. Since FY24 Alkem has spent on new businesses outside its core: Enzene's $50mn biologics plant in New Jersey (opened Sep-2025; runs at a loss of ~₹240 cr a year before revenue), small orthopaedic device companies (Bombay Ortho, Adroit Biomed), up to ₹1,100 cr for 55% of Occlutech (structural heart devices, closed Jul-2026) plus ~₹200 cr to fund it, and treasury money in real estate (₹75 cr written off in Q4FY26).

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, real cash, but recurring "exceptional" items, a big other-income share and a tax holiday that flattered profits

blocks.p: Deloitte gave an unmodified opinion on FY26. Profits convert to cash, though less fully of late (cash from operations after tax was 65% of EBITDA in FY26, 76% in FY25 and 87% in FY24, as inventory and receivables grew), revenue recognition is conventional, and capitalised R&D is small (intangibles under development ₹144 cr). We flag four things. (1) **"Exceptional" items recur**: charges in FY23 (₹173 cr pre-tax), FY24 (₹122 cr) and FY26 (₹175 cr: labour codes ₹113 cr, real-estate impairment ₹75 cr, less a ₹14 cr plant-sale gain). We use EPS before them for the valuation history, but investors should not assume they never come back. (2) **Other income is large**: ₹583 cr in FY26, 19% of PBT before exceptional items, of which ₹85 cr was FX gains. (3) **Tax**: a decade of 9-18% tax rates came from Sikkim holiday units; the income-tax department challenged those deductions (search in Sep-2023), though CIT(A) deleted ₹661 cr of disallowances in Jun-2026; the ₹1,485 cr MAT credit is an asset whose cash value depends on future taxable profit. (4) **Minorities**: 49% of Indchemie and 39% of Cachet belong to others, and 45% of Occlutech from FY27; Screener's "net profit" is before minorities (our patch fixes it).

blocks.p: At Mar-26 Alkem held ₹7,160 cr of cash, bank and NBFC deposits, bonds and funds against ₹1,624 cr of borrowings (mostly overdrafts secured on its own deposits) and ₹424 cr of leases: net cash of ₹5,474 cr on the company's definition, ₹5,764 cr at Jun-26. sections.title: Valuation: 29.5x Sep-28E EPS gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}; the upside is the sector's re-rating, which Alkem has not shared

blocks.p: Every note standing on 30-Sep-2026 that discloses a method for Alkem uses **P/E** except one old one: Motilal Oswal 27x 12-month-forward EPS (15-Aug-2026), Choice 25x FY28E (set May-2026, kept Aug-2026) and BOBCAPS 21x Jun-28E (14-Aug-2026); Nuvama's last public note (Nov-2025) used a sum of the parts. We follow the majority: **P/E on Sep-28E EPS (half FY28E, half FY29E)**, the EPS a buyer will look at one year from now. We use EPS to shareholders (after minorities: ₹30 / 45 / 60 cr in FY27-29E, which the engine cannot separate) and forecast no exceptional items. EV/EBITDA and a DCF are cross-checks only.

The house rule (PLAYBOOK §4, §7c): Alkem's own one-year-forward P/E (price ÷ next full fiscal year's EPS) from Apr-2021 to 30-Sep-2026, every fifth weekly close (58 points), leaving out trough years (none: forward EPS never fell below half of its prior three-year peak; FY23's ₹89.8 was 65% of FY22's ₹138.5); EPS before exceptional items because Alkem booked material exceptional charges in FY23, FY24 and FY26 (A18); then multiplied by the pharma sector factor, the median move of the eight peers' trailing P/E at the 30-Sep-2026 close against their five-year medians (+10.25%, set for Alkem in PLAYBOOK §7c A20; our reproduction +10.3%), and rounded to the nearest half-turn. No own de-rating, growth or returns adjustment enters the base; those are sensitivities below.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good, slow business whose value hinges on getting the sector's multiple; the tax reset and Daman are the near-term tests

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's #1 anti-infectives franchise and #6 drug maker, a 14,500-strong field force, brands that doctors keep prescribing, a US generics business that is flat in dollars, ₹5,764 cr of net cash (~9% of market value), and three options (Enzene biosimilars and CDMO, MedTech/Occlutech, semaglutide) that cost money today. **What you are not buying:** a fast-growing chronic franchise, pricing power in the US, a low tax rate (gone from FY27) or a professional CEO (the seat was empty on 30-Sep-2026).

**What you are paying:** ₹5,164 is 28.6x trailing EPS, 24.5x our FY28E EPS to shareholders and 22.7x Sep-28E, against a 26.6x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021. Pharma peers trade 10.25% above their five-year medians; Alkem 6.6% below. Our target assumes Alkem simply returns to its own median plus the sector's move: 29.5x Sep-28E EPS gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). The DCF (₹4,649) says cash flows alone do not support even today's price; the target, like the sector's prices, rests on the multiple.

FY27E +12.8%: India +11% (Q1 +10.3% with trade generics flat and branded generics +12%; the MD expects ~12% for the year, 'could end up close to 12%', 14-Aug-2026 call; we stay 1pp below because trade generics have grown ~4% a year since the carve-out); US +6% in rupees (Q1 +6.5%; guidance 'high single digit to mid', helped by the weaker rupee; Q2 laps a +33% quarter from the sacubitril-valsartan launch; tolvaptan launch in Q2); other international +18% organic (Q1 +34.5%; guidance 'higher teens'); Occlutech ₹400 cr for ~8.5 months (management target, consolidated from mid-Jul-2026); other operating income ₹90 cr (Q1 ₹20 cr vs ₹52 cr a year earlier as Sikkim GST incentives fade). FY28E +11.6%: India +11%, US +5%, international +15%, a full year of Occlutech (₹650 cr). FY29E +9.9%: India +10.5%, US +4% (price erosion on tolvaptan and FY27 launches; the Daman OAI slows new approvals), international +14%, Occlutech ₹750 cr.

Enzene's US CDMO; other international ₹1,696.4 cr; other operating income ₹179.9 cr = ₹14,712.2 cr). Occlutech (55% owned, consolidated 100% from mid-Jul-2026) is shown as its own line; the company has not said in which line it will report it.

assumptions._marginWhy: Company EBITDA margin (excluding other income): 19.4% FY25, 20.4% FY26 (21.9/23.0/22.2/14.4% by quarter; Q4 carries the year's peak R&D), 20.5% in Q1FY27 (−145bp YoY) despite a ten-year-high 67.9% gross margin, because staff costs rose 17% (1,200 more reps, increments, Enzene US) and other expenses 25% (Enzene US CDMO opex ~₹60 cr a quarter, Occlutech due diligence, the weak rupee on overseas costs). Guidance: 20-21% for FY27 before Occlutech (Q4FY26 call, 28-May-2026); gross margin 66.5-67% for the rest of FY27 as higher-cost API inventory flows through (Q1 call). FY27E 20.0%: the bottom of the range, because Occlutech (₹400 cr at breakeven EBITDA, management) dilutes ~50bp and the US CDMO will not break even within 12 months (MD). FY28E 20.8%: CDMO revenue towards the $25-30mn breakeven run-rate, Occlutech margin +7-8pp a year (CFO), India mix. FY29E 21.3%. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹185 cr of EBITDA (~5% of FY28E EPS).

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Alkem: P/E (MOSL 27x 12-month-forward EPS, Choice 25x FY28E, BOBCAPS 21x Jun-28E; Nuvama's last public note used SOTP). 29.5x Sep-28E EPS to shareholders = Alkem's 26.6x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 on EPS before exceptional items (A18; 26.6x on reported EPS; no trough years) x the pharma sector factor of 1.1025 (median of SUNPHARMA, DIVISLAB, TORNTPHARM, ZYDUSLIFE, CIPLA, AUROPHARMA, IPCALAB, ABBOTINDIA trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians, excluding Alkem: +10.25%, PLAYBOOK §7c A20) = 29.3x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. Bull 34x / bear 22.5x = 75th / 25th percentile (30.7x / 20.5x) x the factor. The engine's EPS includes minorities, so the multiple here is the equivalent on engine EPS: 29.5x x 227.8 / 232.2 = 28.94x. No growth, returns or own-de-rating adjustment (sensitivity rows only).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check. Alkem's median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 is 20.6x (Screener); times the EV/EBITDA analogue of the sector factor (+9.1%, same eight peers) = 22.5x, rounded to 22.5x and applied to trailing EBITDA at the target date (half FY27E + half FY28E) with net cash at Sep-2027. Bull 24x / bear 20.5x = 75th / 25th percentile x the factor.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at an 11.3% cost of equity, terminal growth 5.5%, plus net cash.
